criterion: HW H1.7: cooperative matrix GEMM on tensor cores through VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix, with a portable compute fallback (mission-control 2026-10-10-engine-hw/PLAN.md)
written: 2026-10-10, before the implementation and the first run
kernel: C = A B with A (M x K) and B (K x N) in fp16 row-major, C in fp32 row-major. The tensor-core kernel: one subgroup a workgroup, each subgroup owns a 32 x 32 tile of C as four 16 x 16 fp32 accumulators and loops over K in steps of 16 with coopMatLoad and coopMatMulAdd from global memory. The fallback: 16 x 16 workgroups, a 16 x 16 shared-memory tile each of A and B, fp32 multiply-add of fp16 values unpacked with unpackHalf2x16 (no 16-bit feature needed).
sizes: M = N = K in {1024, 2048, 4096}. Inputs: fp16 values of a seeded uniform draw in [-1, 1].
plan_note: The plan's placeholder bound for H1.7 (2^-20 times the sum of |a||b|) is replaced here before any run: a correct fp32 accumulation over K = 4096 terms has a typical error near sqrt(K) 2^-24 and a worst case near K 2^-24 times that sum, both above 2^-20 for large K.

accuracy.what: every element of the top-left 128 x 128 block and 8,192 seeded random elements, against a float64 dot product of the same fp16 inputs
accuracy.bound: |c - ref| <= K * 2^-23 * sum_k |a_ik b_kj| + 1e-6 on every checked element (the deterministic bound for any summation order of K terms; 2^-23 covers round-toward-zero accumulation, which some tensor-core generations use)
accuracy.reported: the RMS of (c - ref) over the checked elements, divided by the RMS error of a sequential fp32 CPU sum of the same products; reported, not bounded

control_skip_k.what: the tensor-core kernel with the last 16-wide K step skipped

control_layout.what: the tensor-core kernel loading B as column-major

fallback.what: the fallback kernel on the same inputs, and RAW_NATIVE_HW_DISABLE=cooperative_matrix
fallback.bound: the fallback meets the same accuracy bound; with the feature forced off the tool runs only the fallback and says so

timing: GPU timestamps, 10 warm-up and 100 measured dispatches a size on the RTX 4090 (3 on SwiftShader, fallback only, not a claim). Reported: median, p5, p95, p99, IQR and TFLOPS at the median (2 M N K flops). The speedup of the tensor-core kernel over the fallback is the ratio of medians with a 95% bootstrap interval (10,000 resamples); 'faster' needs an interval above 1. No comparison with vendor libraries is made.
adapters: SwiftShader Vulkan locally (no cooperative matrix: the fallback and the forced-off path only); the RTX 4090 only under D:/gpu.lock.d
does_not_prove: Peak tensor-core throughput (the kernel is not tuned: no shared-memory staging, no double buffering); correctness for other types or shapes than those run; anything about D3D12.
method_note_1: Added 2026-10-10 after the first SwiftShader run and before any run of the new control. The two committed controls apply to the tensor-core kernel only, so on an adapter without cooperative matrices nothing showed that the accuracy check can fail. Added: control_fallback_skip_k, the fallback kernel with its last 16-wide K tile skipped; bound: the accuracy bound fails. It runs on every adapter.
